welp you have your word cut out for you here. # Work order — Agent Seat / model editor defects found building `police_sedan`

**Origin:** req_3751 (model a police sedan, 3000 tri budget, no primitive soup).
Everything below was hit during one continuous box-modelling session in the live
editor via `tools/seat`. Follow-ups: req_3756, req_3757, req_3758, req_3759, req_3760.

**State of the live model when this was written:** `police_sedan`, 966 triangles,
`NOT ON DISK` (never saved). The **mesh is sound** — 0 intersecting, 0 degenerate,
0 non-manifold, 90+ named semantic regions, `unnamed: 0`. The **Outliner part rows
are garbage** (see P0-1). Nothing here is a modelling mistake to be re-done; it is a
list of tool defects that shaped, blocked, or corrupted the work.

Verification method used throughout: triangles pulled by index out of the resident
buffer with absolute vertex positions (`follow inspect`), audited by a local
reimplementation of `framework/gpu/mesh_audit.zig`. That path is independent of the
part table, which is why the geometry claims above still hold while the part rows do not.

---

## P0 — Corruption. Fix before any further modelling.

### P0-1. Outliner part-range re-stamp is latched off permanently by a count mismatch

**File:** `cart/editor/shell/AppFrame.tsx:4901`

```js
// A count mismatch means a STRUCTURAL change is mid-flight (append/detach/
// delete) — its own handler adds/removes the row with the op's range.
if (rows.length === 0 || rows.length !== ranges.length) return prev;
```

The host maintains part ranges correctly through every topology op. ModelView
re-reads them (`resyncPartRanges`, `ModelView.tsx:1410`) and announces them through
`__modelPartRangesChanged`. That whole pipeline fires. The shell then **discards the
update** whenever the native part count and the Outliner row count disagree.

This is a latch, not a transient: once the counts diverge, every subsequent re-stamp
is a no-op, and the only thing that could bring the counts back into agreement is the
re-stamp that is being blocked. There is no reconciliation path. **This is why
previous fixes in this area never held** — they addressed drifted ranges rather than
the thing that makes drift permanent.

**Observed end state in this session:** native 19 parts, Outliner 13 rows. Every
single row addressed foreign geometry:

| Outliner row | its range | what it actually addresses |
|---|---|---|
| Body | `[0,269)` | Body(219) + Wheel FR(36) + Wheel RR(14) |
| Wheel FR | `[269,305)` | Wheel RR(22) + Wheel FL(14) |
| Wheel FL | `[341,377)` | Wheel RL(22) + Cabin(8) + Dashboard(6) |
| Wheel RL | `[377,413)` | Console(6) + Partition(6) + Seat FL(14) + Seat FR(10) |
| Cabin | `[413,421)` | Seat FR(4) + Seat Rear(4) |
| Steering Wheel | `[481,517)` | lightbar(4) + mirror(6) + mirror(6) + pushBar(6) + exhaustTip(14) |

Selecting "Cabin" selects a seat backrest and part of the rear bench — not one vertex
of the cabin. Hiding, moving, duplicating or **deleting** any row hits other parts'
geometry.

**Minimal repro (no modelling needed):**
```
tools/seat action viewport '{"operation":"read"}'   # note result.partRanges vs percept.parts
tools/seat --brief select region:<anything on the body>
tools/seat --brief cut 0 1 0.5
tools/seat action viewport '{"operation":"read"}'   # native range moved, row did not
tools/seat undo
tools/seat action viewport '{"operation":"read"}'   # native moved back, row still frozen
```
Measured: native Body `[0,219) → [0,252) → [0,219)`; Outliner Body stayed `[0,269)`
throughout, with `nativeParts=19, rows=13` the whole time.

**Direction:** reconcile rows to native parts by **identity**, not by rank + equal
count. `stampRowsByRank` (`AppFrame.tsx:~4880`) assumes row *N* is native part *N*;
that assumption is what the guard exists to protect and it is the wrong invariant.
Rows need a durable native part key so they can be matched, and orphans on either
side surfaced rather than silently frozen. At minimum the mismatch must be a loud,
recoverable state, never a silent permanent no-op.

### P0-2. `detach` followed by `undo` desynchronises native parts from Outliner rows

What armed P0-1 here. Glazing was detached into its own part (row appeared, part
appeared). A later unrelated `undo` reverted the detach natively but the row did not
come back symmetrically — the session was left with a native part carrying 4 stray
`roof` triangles and no row. From that moment `19 != 13` and P0-1 latched.

Needs an isolated repro and a regression test: any part-structural op (`add`,
`detach`, `part-delete`, `part-merge`) and its undo/redo must leave native parts and
Outliner rows in step, or explicitly reconcile.

---

## P1 — Modelling capability gaps that forced redesigns

*P1-0 is listed first because it is why most of the rest went unnoticed for so long.*

### P1-0. The model stage cannot convey form — modelling through it is effectively blind

**Symptom:** with the vertex/edge overlay off, the car renders as a near-uniform tan
mass. Measured over 164,318 body pixels in a 3/4 view:

```
p5  116.9    p25 116.9    p50 118.2    p75 118.2    p95 149.4
```

**75% of the entire body sits inside a 1.3/255 luminance band** — p25 to p75 differ by
half a percent. 90% sits inside 32.5/255 (12.8% of range). The values are also heavily
quantised into a few flat tones, i.e. per-face flat shading with no gradient across a face.

There *is* a normal term — a top-down view of the roof/hood reads luminance 165.6 vs
118.2 for the flank, a 1.40× ratio — so it is not unlit. But that differentiation does
not survive inside a single view, where adjacent panels at real angle differences land
within ~1% of each other.

**What is not visible in the shaded render** (all of it verified present in the geometry):
wheel arch openings (a 0.71 × 0.50 m hole with a 0.21 m deep well behind it), the fuel
filler door recess, the headlight and taillight pockets, every panel break between
hood / fender / door / quarter, the beltline shoulder tuck, and the arch corner bevels.
None of them read. The greenhouse only reads because glass is a different material.

**Consequence for the session that produced this document:** every shape judgement was
made from the vertex/edge overlay, the numeric bboxes in the percept, and a local
reimplementation of the audit reading absolute triangle positions — **not from looking
at the model.** With the overlay off the mesh is indistinguishable from a box. That is
also why P0-1's part corruption was only caught by the user noticing wrong verts
highlighted, rather than by anything in the render.

**What's missing, in value order:**

1. **No ambient occlusion / cavity term.** `grep -rn "occlusion|matcap|cavity"` over
   `framework/gpu/*.zig` returns nothing but an unrelated comment. This is the single
   highest-value fix: cavity shading is what makes recesses, holes and creases legible,
   and it is exactly why the same mesh reads instantly in Blender's solid mode.
2. **No matcap option.** A matcap alone would restore legibility with zero scene-lighting
   work — the standard DCC answer, and cheap.
3. **Shading ramp too shallow / no specular response on the model stage.** The uniform
   has `light_dir`, `specular_power`, `ambient_color` (`3d.zig:73-77`), so the plumbing
   exists. Worth checking what the model viewport actually feeds it: the scene default
   is `light_dir = {0.577, 0.577, 0.577}` (`3d.zig:13849`) — a light on the box diagonal,
   which is close to the worst possible choice for reading axis-aligned form, since +X,
   +Y and +Z faces then receive near-identical N·L.

**Ask:** cavity/AO or a matcap on the model stage, plus a light direction that separates
the three principal axes. Until then the overlay is not a debugging aid, it is the only
way to see the model at all.

### P1-1. `extrude` accepts exactly one authored face

**File:** `framework/v8_bindings_core.zig:1201-1209` — "Extrude exactly one selected
authored face". `seatApi.extrude` passes straight through.

Selecting a patch of 6 coplanar quads and extruding is rejected. This is the single
biggest constraint on real box modelling — insetting a panel, pushing in a
multi-quad recess, or building a wheel well from an arch region all need it.

**What it cost:** the wheel wells could only be made with one extrude each if each
arch was exactly **one** quad, so the entire longitudinal/height loop layout of the
car had to be re-planned and re-slid around that constraint (14 z-stations and the
height rows chosen so `z -1.83..-1.12 × y 0.28..0.78` was a single quad). That is the
tool dictating the topology instead of the model dictating it.

**Ask:** region/multi-face extrude that extrudes a connected selection as one shell
(shared perimeter walls, no internal walls between the selected faces).

### P1-2. `merge-faces` is a triangle-pair quadifier, not an n-gon builder

**File:** `framework/gpu/indexed_edit_mesh.zig:1595` `mergeSelected` → uses
`sharedTriangleDiagonal` over the selection, i.e. it only handles *two triangles
sharing one diagonal*.

The obvious workaround for P1-1 — merge the patch into one authored face, then
extrude it — does not exist. Selecting 6 coplanar quads returns
`select two or more compatible faces`, which is actively misleading: they *are*
coplanar, adjacent, same winding, and there are more than two.

**Ask:** either genuine n-gon merge for a coplanar connected selection, or a rejection
message that states the real rule ("Merge Faces joins exactly two triangles across a
shared diagonal").

### P1-3. `cut` vs `basic-cut` is undocumented — the wrong one got used all session

**Not a defect — an authoring error caused by a doc gap.** Both verbs exist and
behave completely differently, and the Agent Seat verb table gives no way to tell:

| verb | doc text | actual behaviour |
|---|---|---|
| `cut` | "Loop cut the current face selection" | propagates the edge ring around the whole body |
| `basic-cut` | "Basic cut through the same atomic native session" | subdivides **only the selected faces** |

Measured on an identical selection (`region:hood`, 1 cut, offset 0.5):

```
basic-cut   966 -> 972   (+6)    regions touched: {hood: 6}
cut         966 -> 1032  (+66)   regions touched: {noseTop, hood, windshield, roof,
                                  backlight, trunkLid, underbody, rearFascia, frontFascia}
```

`basic-cut` is precisely the bounded subdivide that was wanted. `cut` got reached for
every time because `basic-cut`'s one-line description says nothing about locality —
and the model paid for it: properly rounded wheel arches were abandoned because
cutting the well roof with `cut` cost 140 triangles, where `basic-cut` costs ~6. The
arches shipped as corner bevels instead, a worse result for no reason.

**Ask:** documentation only. State plainly that `cut` propagates the edge ring while
`basic-cut` subdivides only the selection — in `.claude/skills/agent-seat/SKILL.md`
and in the verbs' own help/reply text. No code change needed.

### P1-4. Cylinder caps are triangle fans, not authored n-gons

`add cylinder ... ; select region:<name>.cap.top` returns 12 faces, so `extrude` and
`inset` both refuse it. Blocked building a steering column out of the wheel hub
(the natural welded construction); the wheel had to ship without a column.

**Ask:** author primitive caps as single n-gon faces, as cube faces already are.

---

## P2 — API correctness / usability defects

### P2-1. `elements` silently truncates at the 64 KB socket cap

At ~600 triangles the whole-mesh `elements` reply hits exactly 65536 bytes and
returns **invalid JSON** (`Unterminated string starting at ... char 65523`). No
error, no `truncated` flag, no paging. This is the primary vertex-position door, so
every position-driven workflow dies at a few hundred triangles — well below the 3000
tri target in the brief.

`elements` also **ignores part scope**: scoping to a 6-face part still returns the
whole mesh, so you cannot dodge the cap that way.

Worked around by building a paged vertex reader on top of `follow inspect` (which
does return **global** vertex ids and pages cleanly). That should be the built-in
behaviour.

**Ask:** page `elements`, or have it honour part scope, or at minimum fail loudly.

### P2-2. Transforms operate on vertex selections, not face selections

`scale` / `move` are rejected (`transform rejected`) when the current selection is a
set of faces; they work when the same geometry is selected as vertices. Nothing in
the Seat docs says this, and the verb table describes transforms as acting on "the
current selection". Cost several failed attempts on wheel scaling before it was
inferred.

**Ask:** document it, or make transforms resolve a face selection to its vertices.

### P2-3. `inset` corrupts silently when face indices go stale between calls

Each `inset` renumbers faces. A batch of insets whose target indices were computed
from one pre-batch fetch applies the later ones to **the wrong quads** and reports
`ok: true`. Produced headlight caps stretched across the car centre and a "taillight"
recess cut into the rear quarter flank.

Second, related trap: reusing one region name across two separate insets makes the
second inset's internal scale drag the **first** inset's cap (the scale resolves
against the shared region). Unique names per instance is a hard requirement, which
collides with P2-4 below.

**Ask:** have `inset` resolve its target stably, and/or return the new face ids so a
caller can re-anchor.

### P2-4. Shared region names + the scope boundary make repeated structures unusable

The Seat doc says "a repeated structure should share one name, not `window1`,
`window2`". But with two seats both named `seatFront`, `select region:seatFront.top`
matches both, the active part scope permits only one, and the selector boundary
(correctly) rejects the partial match. So the documented naming rule cannot be
followed for any repeated part you then want to edit individually.

There is also no compound selector for this — no `region:X & part:Y`, no union of two
regions. Everything non-trivial falls back to `select-elements` with explicit indices,
which then collides with P2-3's staleness.

**Ask:** `region:<name> & part:<id>` (or instance-qualified selection), so shared
names stay legal *and* addressable.

### P2-5. Negative numeric arguments are eaten by the CLI as flags

`tools/seat extrude -0.21 wheelWell` fails with
`extrude rejected (selection, name, or naming debt)` — a misleading message; the real
cause is `-0.21` being parsed as an option. `tools/seat action extrude
'{"distance":-0.21,...}'` works. Affects every verb with a signed numeric arg.

### P2-6. `viewport pose` silently no-ops

`{"operation":"pose","yaw":1.57,"pitch":0}` returns ok and changes nothing; the real
shape is a 6-element `pose` array. Also **pitch sign is inverted** from the obvious
reading — negative pitch puts the camera *below* the model. Cost a wasted round of
"why is my car upside down" shots. Relative `orbit` in degrees works fine.

### P2-7. `selection-mode` error message implies names are accepted

`{"operation":"selection-mode","mode":"face"}` → rejected with
`selection mode must be 0=view, 1=vertex, 2=edge, or 3=face`. The message reads as if
`"face"` is valid. Accept the names, or say "numeric only".

---

## P3 — Measurement / audit defects

### P3-1. `mesh_audit` treats glass as fully opaque

**File:** `framework/gpu/mesh_audit.zig` — `audit()` receives only `verts: []const f32`
and reads **position only**. It never sees per-face material, base colour, or
`model_paint.GLASS_ALPHA` (`framework/gpu/model_paint.zig:114-117`). There is no
exemption and no TODO.

Consequence: **any glazed cabin reports its entire interior as unreachable.** On this
car, 184 of 187 unreachable triangles were cabin content (seats, steering wheel,
dash, console, partition, cabin shell) that is plainly visible through the glass in a
self-shot. The exterior shell had ~0 buried faces.

This matters because "unreachable" is the metric the Agent Seat doc leans on as the
finish gate for "don't ship geometry no camera can see". As it stands the metric
cannot be used on any vehicle or building with windows — exactly the cases where
interiors exist. Hiding the glass part does not rescue it either (rays then have to
thread the window aperture and mostly still fail).

**Ask:** skip glass-alpha faces as ray blockers, or report interior-vs-exterior
separately so the exterior figure stays meaningful.

### P3-2. Audit counts are cached against generation and go stale on transforms

Cache key is `{model hash, generation, face count}`. Pure vertex transforms do not
bump generation, so **moving a solid clean through another solid does not change the
reported counts.** Demonstrated: a probe cube fully enclosed inside the body reported
`32 intersecting`; moving it to genuinely pierce the roof reported `32 intersecting`
— identical, while a correct recomputation gives 0 then 12.

Separately, the `intersecting` figure carried a persistent **+20 phantom** across many
states in this session (editor 20 / independently computed 0; editor 32 / computed 12
— delta correct, baseline wrong). `unreachable` matched an independent implementation
in every state compared. Adjacent to req_3752's "audit facts leaked" class.

**Ask:** invalidate on transform, and find the source of the constant offset.

---

## P4 — Papercuts

- **P4-1.** Deleting a part leaves its regions in the semantic table with 0 faces
  (`probeCube.right` etc. persisted for the rest of the session).
- **P4-2.** Undo stack depth (~32) is too shallow for a modelling session — 160
  `undo` calls rewound only the vertex moves and never reached the loop cuts, so an
  early layout decision could not be revisited.
- **P4-3.** `undo` granularity is surprising: one `undo` intended for a loop cut also
  reverted an earlier `detach`. Undo units do not map to the verbs an agent issued.
- **P4-4.** Some actions (`inset`, `bevel`) return the **entire** percept — full region
  table, all bboxes, all parts, tens of KB — regardless of `--brief`.
- **P4-5.** `part-merge` is documented as changing no geometry (correct), but there is
  no counterpart verb that *does* the junction work (delete mating faces → bridge →
  weld) in one step. Every junction is hand-built; a `join-parts` verb would remove
  the single biggest incentive to leave primitive soup.

---

## What worked well (do not regress)

- Named-region semantics: `unnamed: 0` across 90+ regions, `look` reads like a car.
- The selector boundary refusing partial out-of-scope matches — it caught several real
  mistakes instead of silently moving a subset.
- `inset`'s internal rollback on a rejected scale — clean, left no debris.
- `bevel` on a single vertex.
- `follow inspect` — global vertex ids, pages cleanly, returns part/region/material per
  triangle. This is the reliable read door; `elements` should behave like it.
- Self-shot capture (`tools/seat shot`) — fast and correct every time.

---

## Acceptance for this work order

1. P0-1 repro above shows the Outliner row following the native range through a cut
   and its undo, with a regression test covering `nativeParts != rows`.
2. P0-2 has an isolated repro and a test that `detach` + `undo` leaves parts and rows
   in step.
3. `police_sedan`'s part table can be rebuilt from geometry and every Outliner row
   selects its own solid (verify with the mapping table method used above).
4. P1-1 and P1-2 have either an implementation or a decided, documented answer, since
   between them they dictate how every future model must be topologised.

events.text: User amendment (req_3764): do NOT rescue the live police_sedan — it is a disposable test surface. The reconcile/rebuild-from-geometry path still ships as the P0-1 mismatch recovery mechanism; the live-session rescue choreography is dropped. Zig rebuilds are now unconstrained.

FOLLOW-UPS not closed by this batch: (1) P1-0 substance — the model stage's declared Scene3D light rig provably never reaches the mesh draw (byte-identical self-shots across a key-direction flip; default warm sun renders regardless), so rig plumbing + cavity/AO or matcap remain open; the latent direction inversion is fixed ahead of the plumbing. (2) tools/mesh-port-parity was dead at its reader since the RJMD v4 bump — reader revived this batch, and underneath are real contract divergences that predate this session: basic-cut produces S=1 strips where the reference expects 3..4 on every fixture, pyramid loopcut/loopcutmix diverge, sheared/nonsquare merge differ by hashes only. (3) P2-3 inset stale-index corruption, P2-4 region+part compound selectors, P3-2's +20 intersecting phantom baseline, P4 undo depth/granularity and the join-parts verb. (4) scenario C exposed a transient one-row state right after a native undo that the reconciler heals within its beat — self-healing proven, root cause not yet isolated.

CORRECTION to the earlier follow-up note (req_3765): the model-stage light rig is NOT disconnected — that claim came from a stale-baseline shot comparison (the 'before' binary already contained the direction fix; deterministic headless renders made identical md5s look like proof). Probe builds settle it: the viewer ambient/key rig fully reaches the mesh draw, and the stage light is a separate system from the authored LightRig emitters. The underside-aimed key WAS the P1-0 flatness: visible faces sat at flat 0.65 ambient. With the fixed direction the faces measure 180/156/148 (arithmetic fit predicted 179/157/148) vs flat ~124 under the old key. Light-fix commit amended to 767a2c3fe with the corrected story. Still open for P1-0: cavity/AO or matcap for recess/crease legibility.

resolution: Worked the police_sedan work order end to end. P0-1/P0-2: the Outliner re-stamp latch is dead — a row/range count mismatch now defers one beat and reconciles LOUDLY against host truth (journal-note restore with row identity preserved, else rebuild-from-geometry naming rows by dominant semantic region); the Agent Seat's __mesh_undo bypass and every other native-door path self-heal, and meshUndoRedo refuses stale notes. Regression: tools/part-sync-parity, scenarios A1-A6 + B + C all green, asserting through a partsdump file with row ids proving WHICH recovery path healed. P1-1: region extrude implemented natively — a multi-face selection extrudes as one shell (cap rows copy verbatim so groups/UVs/paint/semantics survive; walls only on the selection boundary; single-face path byte-identical); scenario C pins the exact partition through extrude and undo. P1-2: merge-faces stays a two-triangle quadifier with the honest rule in its reply + docs, region extrude is the multi-face answer. P1-3/P2-2/P2-6/P2-7: cut-vs-basic-cut documented with measured costs, transform replies name real preconditions, viewport pose accepts named fields (was a silent ok-no-op), selection-mode/gizmo accept names. P1-4: cylinder caps are single authored n-gons like the cone base. P2-1: elements honours part scope with global ids. P3-1: the audit sees through glass (unit test pins the sedan shape: interior behind glass 0-unreachable). P3-2: audit cache keys on a verts digest so transforms invalidate. P1-0: found the model-stage key light aimed at the model's UNDERSIDE (shader wants toward-light) — fixed, but byte-identical shots prove the declared rig never reaches the mesh draw at all; rig plumbing + AO/matcap filed as follow-up along with mesh-port-parity's revived-but-diverging contracts (dead at its reader since RJMD v4). Model rescue dropped per req_3764.
